references.text: [ref:Sal 22:1-21|Psalm 22:1-21] is a messianic psalm that prophetically describes the Messiah's sufferings in detail – abandonment, mockery, and the piercing of hands and feet. Jesus points out that Christ had to suffer these things before entering his glory.

[ref:Jes 53:1-12|Isaiah 53:1-12] is the central prophecy about the suffering servant who bears the people's sins, is despised and pierced, but is ultimately exalted. This is exactly what Jesus refers to: the Messiah had to suffer before entering glory.
[ref:Jes 50:6-7|Isaiah 50:6-7] describes the Lord's servant who offers his back to those who strike him and his face to those who spit – a prophecy about Christ's suffering that had to be fulfilled.
[ref:Dan 9:26|Daniel 9:26] prophesies that the anointed one (Messiah) will be cut off – a clear prophecy that Christ had to suffer and die, in line with Jesus' statement that this was necessary.
[ref:Sak 13:7|Zechariah 13:7] prophesies that the shepherd will be struck and the sheep scattered. Jesus refers to the Scriptures' testimony about the Messiah's suffering.
[ref:Jes 11:1-10|Isaiah 11:1-10] describes the Messiah's glory and his coming kingdom – the glory Christ was to enter after his suffering.

[ref:Luk 24:44-46|Luke 24:44-46] confirms the same point: Jesus later explains to the disciples that everything written about him in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms had to be fulfilled, including that the Messiah would suffer and rise from the dead.
[ref:Luk 9:22|Luke 9:22] – Jesus himself predicted that the Son of Man must (ἔδει) suffer greatly, be rejected, be killed, and rise on the third day. The same word of necessity (ἔδει) is used.
[ref:Apg 17:3|Acts 17:3] – Paul preached in the synagogue by explaining from the Scriptures that Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead, exactly the same point Jesus makes on the road to Emmaus.

[ref:1 Pet 1:10-11|1 Peter 1:10-11] says that the prophets searched carefully when and how the Spirit of Christ in them pointed to the sufferings destined for Christ and the glory that would follow – a direct parallel to the suffering-glory sequence in Luke 24:26.
[ref:Fil 2:8-11|Philippians 2:8-11] describes the same divine order: Christ humbled himself and became obedient to death, therefore God exalted him to the highest place. Suffering precedes glory.

[ref:Heb 2:9-10|Hebrews 2:9-10] says that Jesus was crowned with glory and honor because he suffered death, and that it was fitting for God to perfect the author of salvation through sufferings – a theological exposition of the principle in Luke 24:26.
